column1: # content digests — recorded state, not law
# A document whose bytes differ from its recorded digest is DRIFT. Intentional change is a
# two-step act: edit the document, COMMIT it, then --record, and say why in the receipt.
# bind is `committed` (the working tree equals HEAD for that path) or `no-repo` (outside
# version control, so no commit can hold it — counted and named, never silent).
# --record REFUSES a changed document that no commit holds: the working tree differs from
# HEAD, or the document sits outside version control entirely. It keeps the previous row
# and exits 1, so a change the repository does not hold cannot be blessed by re-recording
# the surface. A first pin of an out-of-git document is allowed (nothing is overwritten).
# --record never drops a digest for a file that is gone: it carries the old digest forward,
# so a deletion cannot be laundered by re-recording the surface without it.
